title: Short and long i (ship and sheep)
what: merging /ɪ/ and /iː/, so 'live' and 'leave', 'fit' and 'feet' sound the same
summary: This subtle distinction often goes uncorrected because context usually clarifies meaning. However, merging /ɪ/ and /iː/ can lead to ambiguity and diminish the clarity of your communication, especially in nuanced discussions.
listenFor: Listen carefully to ensure you are consistently differentiating between the short, relaxed /ɪ/ and the long, tense /iː/ in your speech.

contrasts.wrong: The ship were grazing in the field.
contrasts.right: The sheep were grazing in the field.

contrasts.wrong: Please pill the orange for me.
contrasts.right: Please peel the orange for me.
